title: Quoting restoration work with hazard controls priced in
audience: Owners, estimators and leading hands who write quotes for stone and terrazzo restoration
learningOutcomes: List the items a stone restoration quote must show, including the controls and exclusions
Price the wet method, extraction, isolation, test patches and documentation as scope, not as overheads that can be dropped
Write a variation clause for surprises such as a surface that cannot be identified, no water supply or an occupied space.
Explain why a quote does not grant any authority to do regulated work
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: DEWR, Prohibition on the use of engineered stone (no date shown); ASEA, Engineered stone prohibition (no date shown).

instruction.heading: What a stone quote has to show
instruction.body: A quote for stone restoration is a plan of the work, and it should show the scope in terms a client can check. State the surface, the area, the material and finish as far as they are known, and the identification basis. Show the process: assessment, test patch, the honing and polishing sequence, sealing where it is included, cure time and handover. Show the controls as line items: the wet method and water supply, on-tool extraction or ventilation, isolation of the area, the drain and slurry containment, the respiratory protection and health monitoring arrangements where they apply, and the waste disposal. Exclusions must be written down. Typical exclusions include structural repair, cutting and installation, removal of stains that the test patch shows cannot be removed, and any engineered stone work, which this business does not take (“The engineered stone prohibition and what it means on a job”). A quote that prices labour only, and leaves out the controls, is not a valid quote for this work.

instruction.heading: Pricing the controls as scope
instruction.body: The controls take time and equipment, and they must be paid for. The water supply, the extraction, the isolation barriers, the slurry containment and the test patch take time before and after the main work. A specialist rate is earned by pricing the identification, the test, the correct sequence, the sealing and the documentation, not by reducing the controls to make the price look smaller. Use the business pricing method and the minimum charge set in the business policy for site setup and isolation. Where the material costs are passed through, use the materials cost policy. If a competitor's price is lower because it leaves out a control, the quote still needs the control, and the difference should be explained to the client rather than hidden. A price that depends on a control being left out is not a price this business offers.

instruction.heading: Variation clauses for the surprises
instruction.body: Stone jobs produce surprises. The surface may turn out to be engineered stone or may not be confirmed, the water supply may be unavailable, the area may be occupied, or the test patch may show that the finish needs a different and longer sequence. Each of these is a variation. Write the variation rule into the quote: the work stops until the identification is confirmed, the variation is priced in writing and approved before the work resumes, and any extra time or equipment is charged under the variation rate. Do not start unpriced high-hazard work, and do not start work that the variation has not approved. Record each approval.

procedure: Complete the assessment (“Pre-work surface assessment and test patches”) and the identification basis (“Confirm the surface before work: natural stone, terrazzo or engineered stone”) before pricing.
Write the scope: surface, area, material, finish, process, sealing, cure time and handover.
List the controls as line items: wet method, extraction, isolation, containment, respiratory protection and waste disposal.
Add the test patch allowance and the time for the cleaning and documentation.
Write the exclusions, including engineered stone and structural work.
Add the variation clause, with the rule that the work stops and the variation is approved in writing before it resumes.
Obtain the client's written approval of the quote before starting, and file the quote record.

workedExamples.situation: A 60 square metre terrazzo floor in an occupied cafe needs honing and polishing. A competitor has quoted a lower price. The cafe has no water supply near the work area and the owner asks for work to be done after close at a lower rate.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: How should the quote be written, and what is the answer to the lower competing price?
workedExamples.reasoning: The quote must price the water supply or the means to bring water, the isolation of the area, the extraction, the containment and the test patch, and the time they take. The after-close work is priced at its real cost, and the exclusion and variation rules are written in. The competing price is not matched by removing the controls. The owner is told that the lower quote is missing controls the work needs, and the business does not reduce the controls to match it. The quote is not signed by the client until the scope and controls are approved in writing.

equipmentAndPpe: Quote template with scope, controls, exclusions and variation clause
Assessment record and identification basis from “Confirm the surface before work: natural stone, terrazzo or engineered stone” and “Pre-work surface assessment and test patches”
Pricing policy and minimum charge sheet for the business
Client acceptance form or electronic approval

commonErrors.error: Quoting labour only and leaving out the controls.
commonErrors.prevention: List every control as a line item, with its time and cost.

commonErrors.error: Dropping the controls to win the job.
commonErrors.prevention: Controls are part of scope. A quote without them is not a valid quote for this work.

commonErrors.error: Starting work with no variation clause.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the variation rule into the quote and get approval in writing before extra work.

commonErrors.error: Promising a finish before the test patch.
commonErrors.prevention: State the finish as an outcome of the test patch, and quote a test allowance.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: A quote does not grant any licence, permit, notification exemption or authority to do regulated work. Where engineered stone or high-risk silica work may be involved, the quote cannot be accepted for that work until the regulator-compliant route is confirmed in writing by the responsible person.
Stop-work rule: do not start any work that the variation has not approved, and do not start any dusty work that the quote has priced without its controls.
Quotes must not promise results that depend on the surface being confirmed as natural stone or terrazzo, or on a finish that the test patch has not shown is achievable.

qualityStandard: The quote lists every control as a priced line item.
The quote lists exclusions, including engineered stone and structural work.
The variation clause is included and explained to the client.
The client's written approval is on file before work starts.
documentationEvidence: Quote with scope, controls, exclusions and variation clause
Variation records with pricing and approval
Client written approval of the quote
Record of any quote declined or referred because of engineered stone
summary: Show the controls as priced scope, not as optional extras.
Do not match a lower price by removing a control.
Write the exclusions and the variation rule into every quote.
A quote never grants authority to do regulated work.
referencesAtEnd: Official sources to recheck before any job: DEWR, Prohibition on the use of engineered stone (no date shown); ASEA, Engineered stone prohibition (no date shown).

knowledgeChecks.question: What should a stone restoration quote show?
options: Labour only, with no materials or parts
The lowest possible price for the job
Nothing beyond the total price shown
Scope, controls, exclusions and cure time

knowledgeChecks.question: Why should water supply and isolation be priced in the quote?
options: They are controls that take time and cost, and removing them is not a valid saving
They are optional extras that clients can choose to skip or add later on
They apply only to very large quotes and large commercial jobs in the city
Clients always supply them themselves at the start of every single job

knowledgeChecks.question: The surface identification is uncertain at quote stage. What should the quote say?
options: Nothing about it on the quote, the scope or the job at all
That identification is a condition and the variation rule applies
That the surface is granite and polished throughout the job
That the client is responsible for everything on the job

knowledgeChecks.question: Which approach to revenue on specialist stone work is correct?
options: Cutting controls to reduce the cost of the job for the client today
Adding unplanned work without approval from the client or the site today
Pricing identification, test patches, the sequence and documentation as scope
Skipping written approval to save time on the job and the bill today

knowledgeChecks.question: Does completing this lesson or issuing a quote grant the authority to do regulated work?
options: Yes, it grants the authority to do it
Yes, for engineered stone work only at the site
Only in Victoria, under the state rules
No, it grants no licence, permit or authority
